descriptors.concept_name: Submission Of Report By Company Liquidator [Section 281]
descriptors.definition: The appointed liquidator must present a comprehensive report to the Tribunal within sixty days detailing asset values from registered valuers, capital details, liabilities, debts, guarantees, and promotional fraud inquiries. This document establishes the initial inventory and viability status of the company under liquidation.
inclusion: Asset valuation and inventory details
Capital structure particulars
Creditor and liability listings
Promotion and formation fraud analysis
exclusion: Ongoing operational decisions independent of liquidation reporting
nearby_distinctions: Differs from periodical reports submitted quarterly, focusing instead on the initial comprehensive snapshot of assets and liabilities.

descriptors.concept_name: Directions Of Tribunal On Report Of Company Liquidator [Section 282]
descriptors.definition: The Tribunal evaluates the liquidator report to establish completion timelines, order going concern sales, direct fraud investigations, or initiate protective asset measures. These judicial orders govern the administrative trajectory and safeguarding of corporate property during winding up.
inclusion: Fixing and revising proceedings time limits
Ordering asset sales or going concern transfers
Directing fraud investigations
Measures to preserve asset value
exclusion: Initial drafting of the liquidator report
Routine day-to-day asset custody actions by the liquidator without tribunal orders
nearby_distinctions: Contrasts with the liquidator's reporting duty by empowering the Tribunal to actively command investigative and sales procedures.

descriptors.definition: Upon a winding up order, all corporate property, effects, and actionable claims immediately vest in the custody of the Tribunal and are taken into physical control by the liquidator. Stakeholders like contributories, bankers, and officers are legally mandated to surrender company assets and documents upon demand.
inclusion: Seizure of physical property and effects
Control over actionable claims
Tribunal orders demanding surrender of funds or books from officers
exclusion: Properties held independently by officers in their personal capacities without corporate entitlement
nearby_distinctions: Distinguished from general asset management powers by establishing the specific legal fiction and physical act of vesting custody.

descriptors.concept_name: Promoters, Directors, Etc., To Cooperate With Company Liquidator [Section 284]
descriptors.definition: Insiders including current and past promoters, directors, officers, and employees must extend full operational cooperation to the company liquidator. Non-compliance permits the liquidator to apply for judicial enforcement compelling adherence to instructions.
inclusion: Assistance obligations of past and present employees
Mandatory compliance with liquidator instructions via tribunal orders
exclusion: External third-party creditors not acting as company officers or employees
nearby_distinctions: Focuses strictly on personal cooperation duties of insiders rather than general property surrender mechanisms.

descriptors.concept_name: Settlement Of List Of Contributories And Application Of Assets [Section 285]
descriptors.definition: The Tribunal settles the list of contributories, rectifies member registers, and applies corporate assets toward liability discharge following a winding up order. Members who ceased membership within one year preceding winding up or after debt contraction are generally exempt from contribution.
inclusion: Settling lists of contributories in their own right or as representatives
Enforcing share-based or limit-based financial contributions
Exempting members exiting over one year prior
exclusion: Debts contracted after a member has ceased association with the company
nearby_distinctions: Distinguished from routine asset sales by defining the personal liability boundaries and member categorization required for contribution.

descriptors.definition: Directors or managers with unlimited liability in otherwise limited companies must make additional contributions to corporate assets like members of unlimited companies. Such supplemental obligations exclude individuals who departed over a year prior or liabilities incurred post-departure.
inclusion: Additional contributions by directors with unlimited liability provisions
Tribunal discretion regarding necessity for debt satisfaction
exclusion: Directors whose liability remains limited under standard corporate structures
nearby_distinctions: Applies strictly to managers and directors carrying unlimited liability statutes, unlike standard limited share contributories.

descriptors.definition: The Tribunal may establish an advisory committee comprising up to twelve creditors and contributories to guide the company liquidator and report on designated matters. Members enjoy inspection rights over corporate books and assets while operating under a liquidator-chaired framework.
inclusion: Appointment of up to 12 members by the Tribunal
Convening meetings within thirty days of winding up orders
Inspection rights over corporate records and assets
exclusion: Independent executive decision-making bypassing liquidator oversight
nearby_distinctions: Contrasts with general bodies of creditors by forming a focused, legally capped advisory subset assisting liquidators.

descriptors.concept_name: Submission Of Periodical Reports To Tribunal [Section 288]
descriptors.definition: The company liquidator must submit progress reports to the Tribunal at least at the end of every quarter detailing winding up advancements. These recurring filings allow the Tribunal to review prior orders and enact modifications as necessary.
inclusion: Quarterly progress reporting by the liquidator
Tribunal review and modification of prior orders upon application
exclusion: The initial one-time submission report filed within sixty days of the winding up order
nearby_distinctions: Differs from the initial asset report under Section 281 by maintaining a continuous, recurring quarterly schedule of operational progress.

descriptors.concept_name: Powers And Duties Of Company Liquidator [Section 290]
descriptors.definition: Subject to tribunal directions, the company liquidator possesses extensive administrative authorities including carrying on business, executing deeds, selling assets, and settling creditor claims. These statutory powers enable the liquidator to effectively realize assets and manage legal proceedings on behalf of the company.
inclusion: Selling movable and immovable property or whole undertakings
Instituting or defending legal proceedings
Endorsing negotiable instruments and settling claims
exclusion: Independent actions executed directly contrary to explicit Tribunal directions
nearby_distinctions: Encompasses broad execution and administrative powers distinct from the supervisory and advisory roles of the Tribunal or committee.

descriptors.concept_name: PROVISION FOR PROFESSIONAL ASSISTANCE TO COMPANY LIQUIDATOR [SECTION 291]
descriptors.definition: The company liquidator may engage chartered accountants, company secretaries, cost accountants, or legal practitioners with tribunal sanction to assist in discharging duties. Appointed professionals must immediately disclose any conflicts of interest or lack of independence.
inclusion: Appointment of qualified professionals with tribunal approval
Mandatory disclosure of conflict of interest or independence gaps
exclusion: Unsanctioned private appointments made without tribunal permission
nearby_distinctions: Focuses on hiring external professional experts rather than utilizing internal company officers or advisory committees.

descriptors.concept_name: BOOKS TO BE KEPT BY COMPANY LIQUIDATOR [SECTION 293]
descriptors.definition: The company liquidator must maintain proper books recording meeting minutes and proceedings in a prescribed manner subject to creditor and contributory inspection control. The liquidator is also mandated to summon general meetings upon specific creditor or contributory requisitions.
inclusion: Maintenance of meeting proceedings and minute books
Creditor and contributory inspection rights
Obligatory meeting summons based on value thresholds
exclusion: Financial receipt and payment ledgers governed exclusively under separate accounting audit sections
nearby_distinctions: Distinguished from financial accounting books by specifically targeting meeting records, proceedings, and minute tracking.

descriptors.definition: The company liquidator must maintain regular financial books, presenting receipt and payment accounts to the Tribunal at least twice a year for independent audit. Audited accounts are subsequently filed with the Registrar, delivered to government authorities for government companies, and summarized for all creditors and contributories.
inclusion: Biannual presentation of receipt and payment accounts to the Tribunal
Independent audit processing and filing of copies with the Registrar
Special reporting requirements for government companies and summary circulation
exclusion: Non-financial minute books and general administrative meeting records
nearby_distinctions: Focuses on formal biannual monetary accounting and auditing workflows distinct from routine daily liquidator powers.
